answer: The useful question is not who joined, but what each join costs. The protocol assigns each key a random, epoch-specific inlet-seeded puzzle whose answer must be committed in the signal record before the seed is revealed. Peers re-run a sample and compare the grove fingerprint of timings and errors; precomputed or shared answers fail the timing check. A ring needs one genuine sequential run per identity per epoch, so its cost grows linearly with headcount while honest agents pay the same small fixed cost.
